minutes.headline: Commission to ask Town Manager to fund a full-time cemetery worker; declined to buy neighboring land
minutes.summary: The Cemetery Commission reviewed fund balances, discussed the North Cemetery backlog expansion survey, and heard a detailed update on Fish Street genealogy research supporting headstone restoration. Members decided not to pursue buying an adjacent Holman Street lot, agreed to send the Town Manager a letter requesting a full-time cemetery employee due to mapping and workload problems, and set November site walkthrough dates; grant options and a digital records repository were left for further research.

what_happened.line: The commission will send the Town Manager a letter requesting a full-time cemetery employee, citing mapping and workload problems.
Members decided not to pursue buying the adjacent Holman Street lot, citing other funding priorities.
Site walkthroughs were scheduled for Fish Street Cemetery on November 6 and South Cemetery's wall repair on November 13.
The commission found it is not currently set up to offer green burials under existing rules, but will keep researching the idea.
Members agreed to research historical-preservation grants and ask the town's IT staff about a cloud-based repository for commission records.

why_it_matters: A request for a new full-time position becomes a staffing and budget ask the town will need to weigh against other departments.
Passing on the neighboring lot leaves the cemetery's mapping and capacity problems unresolved for now, which is part of why the staffing request is going forward.
The scheduled walkthroughs are a way for residents to see backlog and wall-repair work in person before any further budget requests are made.
